identity: SCRIPTURE - the complete Surat al-Mulk (Quran 67), all 30 ayat, in Uthmani orthography with diacritics and verse markers stripped (سموت، الحيوة، بمصبيح، للشيطين، الأفدة، ءأمنتم، صفت). 333 tokens, ZERO <NL>.
law: THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (0k), fifth scripture document and third Quranic sura. 333 tokens / 30 ayat = 11.1 tokens per verse, min 5, max 18. Inside a verse NOTHING cuts.
reasoning: The sura rhymes almost entirely in -ir / -ur, and reading the rhyme off the line is the whole method (2c): qadir, al-ghafur, futur, hasir, al-sair, al-masir, tafur, nadhir, kabir, al-sair, al-sair, kabir, al-sudur, al-khabir, al-nushur, tamur, nadhir, nakir, basir, ghurur, wa-nufur, mustaqim, then the tashkurun / tuhsharun / sadiqin / mubin / taddaun / alim / mubin / main tail. Three of the rhyme words repeat close together - al-sair at vv. 5, 10 and 11, kabir at vv. 9 and 12, nadhir at vv. 8 and 17, mubin at vv. 26 and 29 - and each is taken in sequence; the last one lands exactly on the final token, which is the alignment proof. Everything else was suppressed: the imperative chains fa-rji al-basar (v.3) and thumma rji al-basar (v.4), which are two SEPARATE verses even though thumma joins them and my old table would either merge or over-cut them; fa-mshu fi manakibiha wa-kulu min rizqihi inside v.15; wa-asirru qawlakum aw ijharu bihi inside v.13; the four qul verses (23, 24, 26, 28, 29, 30), where qul is an announcer and does NOT end its unit here because the whole utterance is one verse; bal at v.21; the twin rhetorical questions of v.22 (a-fa-man yamshi mukibban ... am-man yamshi sawiyyan), which E1 parallelism would split and which are ONE verse; and the reported dialogue of vv. 8-9 (a-lam yatikum nadhir | qalu bala qad jaana nadhir), where the question ends one verse and the answer opens the next - the one place where the verse law and a Q-then-A reading agree.
